taggedLibrary.text_content: Articles of Association of the Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM), registered in Türkiye as a nonprofit organisation with legal personality. Statutes filed with the Ministry of Interior under reg. no. 34-12345.

Independent auditor's report by KPMG Türkiye on the audited annual financial statements of CSIM for the year ended 31 December 2024. The financial statements are prepared in accordance with IFRS for SMEs. We have not identified any audit qualifications. Annual turnover: EUR 920,000. Operating budget: EUR 880,000.

This is to certify that the Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM) successfully delivered the project 'Independent Media in Syria 2021-2024' under SIDA funding (Reference 12345-2021). All milestones were achieved on time and within budget. We confirm satisfactory performance and recommend CSIM for future donor partnerships.

CSIM strategic plan 2025-2027. Our work in Syria covers independent journalism training, editorial coaching for newsrooms in exile, journalist protection programmes including digital security training, and multi-platform content production in Arabic and Kurdish. Logical framework included for the protection of journalists and bloggers under media freedom pillar.

Curriculum Vitae — Jad K., Project Director, CSIM. 12 years experience in Syrian media development, project management of EU and SIDA funded projects, key personnel role on three sub-million EUR grants. Languages: Arabic, English, Turkish.
CSIM safeguarding policy covering prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEA / SEA-H). Compliant with the EU sea-h self-evaluation questionnaire and CHS standards. Updated 2025.

output.executive_summary:
The Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM), a Syrian-led nonprofit registered in Türkiye with operational field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli, submits this concept note as lead applicant for Lot 3 of EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY — Promotion of and Support to Media Freedom and Pluralism in Syria. CSIM's founding mandate, operational geography, and seven-year track record of independent journalism training, journalist protection, and information-integrity programming across Syrian governorates place it in a uniquely strong position to deliver the objectives of this lot. The organisation's network of vetted Syrian journalists, photographers, and fact-checkers, combined with multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish content production capacity, directly addresses the call's three priority areas: strengthening independent media, protecting journalists and media workers, and building public awareness of media freedom.

CSIM brings a demonstrated record of responsible grant stewardship that directly matches EU procurement expectations. Four sub-million-EUR grants from SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews have been delivered on time and without audit qualification, with financial oversight confirmed by a clean KPMG Türkiye audit in 2024. The organisation maintains EUR-denominated banking through Akbank, has a documented safeguarding and PSEA policy, and reports against EU and US humanitarian frameworks. A SIDA bridge-financing letter is available to support co-financing obligations, and CSIM can contribute approximately 5% of total eligible costs from its own reserves, meeting the minimum 10% co-financing threshold when combined with a confirmed EU-eligible co-applicant partner.

The key win-themes for this proposal are: Syrian-led ownership and deep contextual legitimacy; an established field presence in the most media-vulnerable Syrian governorates; a proven multi-donor compliance record; and a proposed programme design that integrates journalist safety, editorial independence, and public media-literacy into a coherent, measurable results chain. CSIM intends to identify and onboard one EU-eligible co-applicant organisation to strengthen co-financing capacity, broaden geographic reach, and reinforce cross-cutting thematic coverage including gender equality and minority rights — areas where CSIM will document existing practice and formalise commitments within the full application.
technical_approach: Context Analysis and Needs Assessment: CSIM's intervention departs from a rigorous, evidence-based analysis of the Syrian media environment following the fall of the Assad regime on 8 December 2024. The transitional period has created both an unprecedented opening for independent media and acute new risks: legacy state media infrastructure remains largely intact, armed actors retain influence over information flows in several governorates, and Syrian journalists — many operating from exile in Türkiye, Iraq, and Lebanon — face continued threats including digital surveillance, harassment, and physical danger when attempting to return or report from inside Syria. CSIM's field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli provide direct access to journalist communities in Northwest Syria, the Kurdish-administered northeast, and the diaspora, enabling a granular needs assessment that will be conducted in the first eight weeks of the action through structured interviews, focus groups with media workers, and a rapid mapping of existing media-support actors to avoid duplication and identify complementarity.

Intervention Logic and Results Chain: The action is structured around three interlocking result areas that directly correspond to the Lot 3 priorities. Result Area 1 (Strengthening Independent Media) targets Syrian newsrooms and individual journalists with editorial coaching, digital-security training, and editorial-standards mentoring, producing measurable improvements in editorial independence and professional practice. Result Area 2 (Journalist Protection) delivers a systematic protection programme including safety assessments, emergency-response protocols, legal-support referrals, and psychosocial first aid for journalists, bloggers, and media workers at risk. Result Area 3 (Public Awareness on Media Freedom) uses CSIM's multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish content production capacity to reach Syrian audiences inside the country and in the diaspora with accessible, culturally resonant messaging on the importance of press freedom, media pluralism, and citizens' right to information. Each result area is linked to specific outputs, outcome indicators, and impact pathways, forming a clear logical framework that will be presented in full in the Annex A.2 application.

Methodology — Journalist Training and Editorial Coaching: CSIM will deploy its established methodology of embedded editorial coaching, in which experienced Syrian editors work alongside newsroom teams over sustained periods rather than delivering one-off workshops. This approach, refined through SIDA-funded programming between 2021 and 2024, has demonstrably improved editorial standards and reduced self-censorship in partner newsrooms. Under this action, CSIM will select up to twelve Syrian media outlets — prioritising those operating in underserved governorates and those led by or significantly employing women journalists — for a twelve-month embedded coaching cycle. Coaching will cover editorial independence, source verification, fact-checking protocols, conflict-sensitive reporting, and digital-security hygiene. CSIM's network of vetted Syrian journalists and photographers will serve as peer-learning facilitators, embedding local ownership and sustainability from the outset.

Methodology — Journalist Protection Programme: CSIM will establish a structured Journalist Protection Unit within the action, building on its existing relationships with Syrian journalist networks and its documented safeguarding framework. The unit will conduct individual safety assessments for at-risk journalists using a standardised risk-matrix tool, provide emergency small grants for relocation or legal support where threats are acute, and maintain a 24-hour referral pathway to partner legal-aid and psychosocial-support providers. CSIM will develop and disseminate a bilingual (Arabic/Kurdish) Digital Security Toolkit tailored to the Syrian operating environment, covering encrypted communications, device security, and online harassment response. The protection programme will be designed with a gender-sensitive lens, recognising that women journalists and LGBTQ+ media workers face compounded risks, and will include dedicated sessions on gender-based online harassment and safety planning.

Methodology — Information Integrity and Anti-Disinformation: CSIM's information-integrity programming will address the proliferation of disinformation in the Syrian information space, which poses a direct threat to media freedom by undermining public trust in independent journalism. The action will support a network of trained Syrian fact-checkers — drawn from CSIM's existing contributor pool — to monitor, verify, and publicly debunk false narratives circulating on social media and in legacy media. CSIM will develop a quarterly Syrian Media Integrity Report, published in Arabic and English, documenting disinformation trends, media-ownership patterns, and threats to editorial independence. This output directly serves the call's public-awareness priority and will be disseminated to Syrian civil society, international donors, and EU institutions.

Partnership and Co-Applicant Strategy: CSIM intends to enter the full application with one EU-eligible co-applicant organisation, to be identified and contracted by 30 September 2025. The co-applicant will be selected on the basis of: complementary geographic reach inside Syria; demonstrated capacity to contribute co-financing of at least 5% of total eligible costs; and thematic expertise in one or more cross-cutting areas (gender equality, disability inclusion, minority rights, or youth engagement) where CSIM seeks to strengthen its programme design. Candidate organisations include European media-development NGOs with existing Syria portfolios and Syrian diaspora organisations with legal personality in EU member states. The partnership agreement will be formalised through a co-applicant declaration and a detailed partnership protocol annexed to the full application.

Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Framework: CSIM will implement a results-oriented M&E framework aligned with EU standard indicators for media-freedom programming. A dedicated M&E Officer will be recruited within the first month of the action to establish baseline data, manage the indicator tracking system, and coordinate quarterly internal reviews. The framework will include output-level indicators (e.g. number of journalists trained, number of safety assessments conducted, number of fact-checks published), outcome-level indicators (e.g. percentage of trained journalists reporting improved editorial-independence practices, percentage of at-risk journalists with active safety plans), and a mid-term and final external evaluation. CSIM will submit six-monthly narrative and financial reports to the contracting authority in the format specified in the grant contract, drawing on its established reporting practice against EU and US humanitarian frameworks.

Quality Assurance and Risk Management: CSIM will apply a three-tier quality-assurance system: internal editorial review by the Executive Director and Senior Programme Manager; peer review by an independent Syrian media expert drawn from CSIM's advisory network; and external audit by KPMG Türkiye on an annual basis. Key risks identified for this action include: deteriorating security conditions in target governorates (mitigated by flexible field-node model and remote-delivery contingency); restrictions on media operations by transitional authorities (mitigated by CSIM's established relationships with transitional government interlocutors and its non-partisan editorial positioning); and co-financing shortfall (mitigated by SIDA bridge-financing letter and active co-applicant recruitment). All risks will be documented in a live risk register updated quarterly and shared with the contracting authority.

output.cover_letter_draft:
18 May 2026

To the Evaluation Committee,
European Union Delegation to Syria
Contracting Authority: European Commission
Call for Proposals Reference: EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY
Lot 3: Promotion of and Support to Media Freedom and Pluralism in Syria

Dear Members of the Evaluation Committee,

The Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM) is pleased to submit this concept note in response to the European Commission's Call for Proposals EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY, specifically for Lot 3: Promotion of and Support to Media Freedom and Pluralism in Syria. CSIM is a Syrian-led nonprofit organisation registered in Türkiye, founded in 2018, with a mandate to strengthen independent journalism, protect media workers, and advance information integrity across Syrian governorates. Our operational field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli, combined with a network of over forty vetted Syrian journalists, photographers, and fact-checkers producing content in Arabic and Kurdish, position CSIM as a uniquely qualified lead applicant for this lot. We are deeply committed to the European Union's objective of contributing to the sustainable and equitable development of Syrian communities and to the full enjoyment of human rights by all, and we believe that a free, pluralistic, and protected media environment is foundational to Syria's transitional recovery.

CSIM's proposed action, titled Voices for a Free Syria: Strengthening Independent Media, Protecting Journalists, and Building Public Awareness of Media Freedom in the Syrian Transition, directly addresses all three priorities of Lot 3. We will deliver embedded editorial coaching to twelve Syrian newsrooms, operate a structured Journalist Protection Unit providing safety assessments, emergency support, and digital-security tools to at-risk journalists and media workers, and produce a bilingual Arabic and Kurdish public-awareness programme — including a quarterly Syrian Media Integrity Report — to build Syrian citizens' understanding of and demand for media freedom. Our methodology is grounded in seven years of direct programming experience, refined through four successfully completed grants from SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews, all delivered on time and confirmed by a clean KPMG Türkiye audit in 2024. We will implement this action in partnership with one EU-eligible co-applicant organisation, to be confirmed at full application stage, ensuring the co-financing threshold is met and cross-cutting thematic coverage — including gender equality, minority rights, and youth engagement — is comprehensively integrated.

We respectfully request that the Evaluation Committee consider this concept note for pre-selection and invite CSIM to submit a full application. We are fully committed to the transparency, accountability, and EU values standards required under this call, and we stand ready to provide any additional documentation or clarification the contracting authority may require. We would also welcome the opportunity to attend the information session scheduled for 21 April 2026 and have registered accordingly. We thank the European Commission and the EU Delegation to Syria for this important initiative and for the opportunity to contribute to Syria's media freedom and democratic transition.

Yours sincerely,

[Name of Executive Director / Authorised Representative]
Executive Director
Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM)

financial_template_notes: Grant amount for Lot 3 is fixed at EUR 675,000 (minimum and maximum are equal). The budget must be designed to exactly match this figure as the EU contribution, with co-financing of at least EUR 75,000 (10% of total eligible costs of EUR 750,000) from non-EU sources. CSIM's own reserves can contribute approximately EUR 37,500 (5%); the remaining co-financing must be confirmed from the co-applicant

At the 90% EU co-financing rate applicable to CSIM as a Türkiye-registered entity, total eligible costs of the action must be approximately EUR 750,000. Budget lines should be constructed to reach this total, with the EU grant covering EUR 675,000 and co-financing covering EUR 75,000. Do not exceed or fall below EUR 675,000 as the EU grant request, as the fixed amount allows no flexibility.

Key cost line items to include: (1) Personnel costs — Executive Director (part-time), Senior Programme Manager, M&E Officer, Field Coordinators in Gaziantep/Erbil/Qamishli, editorial coaches, protection unit staff; (2) Subcontracts — co-applicant activities, external evaluator, KPMG annual audit; (3) Travel and subsistence — field visits, journalist training workshops, information-session attendan

Personnel costs must be calculated on the basis of actual monthly salaries documented in CSIM's payroll records, pro-rated to the percentage of time allocated to the action. Time-sheets will be required for all staff charged to the grant. Ensure that salary levels are consistent with CSIM's existing pay scales as evidenced in the KPMG audit, to avoid audit risk.

All costs must be incurred and paid during the implementation period of the action. Costs incurred before the grant contract signature date are not eligible unless specifically authorised by the contracting authority. Build a realistic implementation timeline that begins activities only after contract signature.

Taxes, including Turkish VAT, are generally not eligible costs under EU grants unless CSIM can demonstrate it is legally obliged to pay them and cannot recover them. Consult the PRAG and the contracting authority's guidance on tax eligibility for Türkiye-registered entities before finalising the budget.

Include a contingency note in the financial narrative (not as a budget line) acknowledging that the fixed grant amount leaves no room for budget overruns. Risk mitigation should include a 3-5% internal management reserve within the co-financing contribution to absorb minor cost variances without requiring a contract amendment.

Co-financing contributions from CSIM's own reserves and the co-applicant must be documented with a co-financing declaration and, where applicable, a letter of commitment from the co-applicant's authorised representative. The SIDA bridge-financing letter should be included as supporting evidence of co-financing availability.

Ensure that no EU general budget or European Development Fund money is used as co-financing. SIDA funding (Swedish bilateral ODA) is eligible as co-financing provided it is not routed through the EU budget. Confirm this with SIDA before citing the bridge-financing letter in the application.

At full application stage, prepare the budget in the format specified in Annex A.2 and the contracting authority's budget template. Ensure all cost lines are justified in the budget narrative with reference to specific activities in the work plan, and that the intervention logic (inputs to activities to outputs) is clearly traceable in the budget structure.
